tasks.task: Pick the right statistical test for a question

items.when: When there is a question and some data and the method is not yet chosen
When you need the test, its assumption checks and effect sizes written up
When you want a second opinion on the design and what the numbers can prove
When the answer is a p-value nobody can read, to say what is known and unknown plainly

tasks.task: Write a checked analysis of a dataset

items.when: When someone asks whether the numbers really show what they think
Before any test, to map the data's structure, spread, links and odd spots
When trends, outliers and correlations need working out and explaining plainly
When the question is what drives an outcome and a fitted model with checks is needed
When reviewers should see every assumption and how it could change the answer
Before the analysis is shared, to check the method, the maths and any bias

tasks.task: Estimate the sample size and run time a test needs

items.when: Before an A/B test or split email, to see if it can find the change you care about
When the design is not a simple two-group test and needs power worked out
When you have visits and orders, to cross-check the size and the weeks needed

tasks.task: Design an A/B test or small trial

items.when: When a change needs one primary metric, a smallest effect and a written plan
When someone wants to test a change and you need the steps from idea to decision
When you want a second plan with its own hypothesis and reading rule to compare
When groups or run order must be set at random so results are not confounded
When two ads, emails or pages are compared and need one change and a winner rule

tasks.task: Plan a price test or an email test queue

items.when: When a price change needs three outcome cases and a test that can be undone
When email flows need a ranked test queue with sample sizes and win rules
When the plan is drafted, to confirm the metric, the effect size and the stop rule

tasks.task: Read a finished test and say whether it won

items.when: When a test has finished and someone wants to ship the winner
When the read-out needs the effect as a range and a plain ship or hold call
When you have the raw test data and need a split check and confidence ranges
When you want the result worked a second way to see if the call holds
When only summary numbers exist, to judge whether the result can be trusted
When tests finish often and each needs the same checked read-out

tasks.task: Design a holdout or lift test for marketing spend

items.when: When a channel or change is doubted and needs a holdout design and run time
When spend runs across regions and a lift test must be sized to the business
When the design is drafted, to check the metric and how the result will be read

tasks.task: Review a result or claim someone handed you

items.when: When a report, chart or claim needs its data, method and conclusion checked
When the claim rests on a study, to grade its biases, flaws and weak statistics
When the report mixes results and hopes, to mark each line proven, likely or a guess
When a number is impressive, to check selection, mechanism and what it can establish

tasks.task: Explain a model or score in plain words

items.when: When a business relies on a score and nobody can say what it means or costs
When you have the trained model and need which inputs matter and where it fails
When single predictions must be explained, with checked plots of what drove each
When the explainer is drafted, to find the jargon and put it in business words

tasks.task: Work out what a model's results table really means

items.when: When you have counts of what was flagged and what really happened
When each kind of mistake has a cost and the decision is whether to use the model
When several models could be used, to rank them with tests that show real differences
When the model was built by someone else and needs a test plan and rated findings

tasks.task: Check a vendor's AI accuracy claim

items.when: When a pitch claims an accuracy figure and you need the questions that test it
When the vendor has answered and the claim must be judged for this business
When the tool is for hiring or staff, to test accuracy and bias and plan a pilot
Before signing, to flag data-training, liability and model-change terms

tasks.task: Design a simple scoring rule to use in place of a model

items.when: When you have ten or twenty cases, to find a one-line rule and test it on unseen ones
When leads need a fit and activity score and ranked tiers
When accounts need a health score and a churn risk from data already held
When orders need fraud rules and a review routine, not a black-box score
When the rule has run on past cases, to count its hits and misses
When people trust gut feel over a rule, to compare past cases and base rates

tasks.task: Pilot an AI tool before the client commits

items.when: When a vendor offers a tool and the client is deciding whether to buy
When the tool writes answers, to set scores, human review and a baseline first
When the pilot is done, to weigh results, costs and harms and choose grow or stop
When results are in, to get an evidence brief and the data gaps flagged
When the go or stop call must be checked against the baseline and a checklist

tasks.task: Write a one-page model card

items.when: When a model is in use and needs an honest record of what it does and how it is watched
When the card needs a plain account of how the model was built and its limits
When the card must name risks, the rules that apply and conditions of use

tasks.task: Run a responsible-AI check on a tool that scores people or money

items.when: When a tool scores, ranks or decides about people and its use must be mapped and tested
When the client works in the EU and needs the risk tier and duties that follow
When risks should be mapped, measured and managed under a named framework
When the tool is used in hiring and needs a policy, a bias check and a staff notice
When the check looks only at accuracy, to start from the people the tool affects
Before the tool decides anything alone, to set a signed human review step

tasks.task: Run a health check on a model the business relies on

items.when: Each quarter, and straight after a complaint or a big change in the data
When the model's rates need baselines and alerts for unusual change
When the health check needs an outside audit with rated findings

tasks.task: Build and validate a predictive model

items.when: When a model is justified and needs a repeatable path from data prep to checks
When there are many columns and the useful inputs must be chosen and tested
When the question is when something happens and some cases have not ended yet
When results look too good or too bad, to find silent bugs before tuning
When the model misbehaves, to look at real examples and start from the smallest case

tasks.task: Estimate an effect when the data is thin

items.when: When there are few data points and the answer should come with honest ranges
When prior knowledge goes in, to state it in plain units and test it makes sense
When the model is fitted, to learn where its results can and cannot be trusted

tasks.task: Forecast a number with honest ranges

items.when: Before forecasting, to find trend, season and odd spikes in the history
When you need a forecast with ranges and a test on held-back data
When a forecast is one confident number, to add base rates and a date to score it

tasks.task: Find natural groups in customer or case data

items.when: When groups should come from behaviour, each profiled with a plan
When groups are found, to test whether the differences between them are real

tasks.task: Test how accurate an AI assistant's answers are

items.when: When an AI feature needs scores, human review and a rule that flags a drop
When answers will be graded by an AI and need a fair scoring guide
When an agent is near release and needs a test set and a decision memo

tasks.task: Write up the method, limits and uncertainty

items.when: When the analysis is done and needs question, data, method, results and rerun steps
When non-specialists must follow how it was done and where it stops
When someone else must repeat the work from a data inventory and method notes
When a range must be explained to an owner, to use comparisons people understand
Before it goes out, to replace statistical terms with plain business words

always.when: Before any analysis, when the decision and the cost of being wrong are not stated
Before any conclusion is sent, to separate what the data shows from what is assumed

helpers.when: When exports must be cleaned and merged before any test can be run
When a site test must be set up, run and tracked in a testing tool
When the question is which channel earns its spend and tracking data must be reconciled
When a model or AI feature must be built into a product and kept running
When an AI tool's use raises legal duties on privacy, hiring or lending
When an AI assistant's accuracy problem lies in its prompts and test set

gaps: No library item works out precision, recall and the cost of each mistake from a table of counts and a base rate; only the kit prompt does
No library item lists the questions to ask about a vendor's AI accuracy claim outside hiring tools
No library item writes a model card
No library item checks a live business model for drift, calibration and performance by group
No library item tests a model's results for unfair differences between groups of people
No library item covers stopping rules, peeking and many comparisons in one test
No library item estimates cause and effect from data that was not a planned test, such as before and after with a comparison group
No library item explains a confidence range or a p-value to an owner in plain words
No library item builds a points-based scoring rule and checks it against past outcomes
No library item reads survey results with margins of error and small-group warnings
